paragraphs: Avista Corp., incorporated in the territory of Washington in 1889, is primarily an electric and natural gas utility with certain other business ventures. Our corporate headquarters is in Spokane, Washington, the second-largest city in Washington. Spokane serves as the business, transportation, medical, industrial and cultural hub of the Inland Northwest region (eastern Washington and northern Idaho). Regional services include government and higher education, medical services, retail trade and finance. Through our subsidiary AEL&P, we also provide electric utility services in Juneau, Alaska.
As of December 31, 2025, we have two reportable business segments as follows:

• Avista Utilities – an operating division of Avista Corp., comprising the regulated utility operations in Washington, Idaho, Oregon and Montana. Avista Utilities provides electric distribution and transmission, and natural gas distribution services in parts of eastern Washington and northern Idaho. Avista Utilities also provides natural gas distribution service in parts of northeastern and southwestern Oregon. Avista Utilities has electric generating facilities in Washington, Idaho, Oregon and Montana. Avista Utilities also supplies electricity to a small number of customers in Montana. Avista Utilities also engages in wholesale purchases and sales of electricity and natural gas as an integral part of energy resource management and its load-serving obligation.
• AEL&P – a regulated utility providing electric services in Juneau, Alaska that is a wholly-owned subsidiary and the primary operating subsidiary of AERC.

We have other businesses, including venture fund investments, real estate investments, as well as certain other investments made by Avista Capital, which is a direct, wholly-owned subsidiary of Avista Corp. These activities do not represent a reportable business segment and are conducted by various direct and indirect subsidiaries of Avista Corp.
Total Avista Corp. shareholders' equity was $2.7 billion as of December 31, 2025, which includes a $126 million investment in Avista Capital and a $129 million investment in AERC.
See "Note 24 of the Notes to Consolidated Financial Statements" for information with respect to the operating performance of each business segment (and other subsidiaries).
On December 31, 2025, Avista Utilities employed 1,929 individuals with bargaining unit employees comprising 36 percent of our overall workforce.

Our approach to people is a critical strategy to inspire engaged and thriving employees by empowering a high-performing organization where employees are valued, respected and have opportunities to grow. Among other things, this strategy supports hiring talented people and equipping them with capabilities, tools and a culture that empowers them to pursue great ideas. Such ideas engage the imagination, stretch us all as we continue to provide exemplary and cost-effective service to our customers. Focus areas for this strategy strive to:
• improve employee engagement, belonging, equity, attraction and retention while building a sense of community and purpose,
• support safety and well-being through innovative programs, best practices, tools, and technology, and
• expand innovation disciplines, capabilities, and mindsets with cross-departmental interactions and external networks to build the utility of the future.
The following is an overview of some of our key human capital initiatives intended to inspire engaged and thriving employees and other stakeholders, such as our customers and business partners.

paragraphs: The following factors could have a significant impact on our operations, results of operations, financial condition or cash flows. These factors could cause future results or outcomes to differ materially from those discussed in our reports filed with the SEC (including this Annual Report on Form 10-K), and elsewhere. See "Forward-Looking Statements" for additional factors which could have a significant impact on our operations, results of operations, financial condition or cash flows and could cause actual results to differ materially from those anticipated in such statements. Additional risks and uncertainties not presently known to us or that we currently do not consider material could also adversely affect us. The realization of many of the risks discussed herein depends upon the prior occurrence of some event or circumstance – i.e. a "trigger". We may or may not discuss the occurrence of a trigger that has not resulted in an adverse effect on us, and the absence of such disclosure should not be construed as a representation that no such trigger has occurred.

Avista Utilities' annual operating expenses and the costs associated with incremental investments in utility assets continue to grow at a faster rate than revenue. Our ability to recover these expenses and capital costs depends on the adequacy and timeliness of retail rate increases allowed by regulatory agencies, as well as managing costs. We expect to periodically file for rate increases with regulatory agencies to recover our expenses and capital costs and provide an opportunity to earn a reasonable rate of return for shareholders. If regulators do not grant rate increases or grant substantially lower rate increases than our requests in the future or if recovery of deferred expenses is disallowed, or if regulators do not allow us to recover costs associated with assets required to be retired or divested to comply with emerging laws and regulations, it could have a negative effect on our financial condition, results of operations or cash flows. See further discussion of regulatory matters in "Item 7. Management's Discussion and Analysis – Regulatory Matters."
If we could no longer apply regulatory accounting principles, we could be: • required to write off our regulatory assets, and be

• precluded from the future deferral of costs or decoupled revenues not recovered through rates at the time such amounts are incurred, even if we expect to recover these amounts from customers in the future.
See further discussion at "Note 1 of the Notes to Consolidated Financial Statements – Regulatory Deferred Charges and Credits."

Our equipment may be the ignition source, or alleged cause of ignition, for wildfires and in the event of a fire caused by our equipment, we could potentially be held liable for resulting damages to life and property, as well as fire suppression costs. Also, wildfires could lead to extended operational outages of our equipment while we wait for the wildfire to be extinguished before restoring power, and the cost to implement rapid response or repair to such facilities could be significant. Wildfires caused by our equipment could cause significant damage to our reputation, which could erode shareholder, customer and community satisfaction. In addition, wildfires caused by our equipment could lead to increased litigation and insurance costs, loss of insurance coverage, the need to be self-insured or the need to consider non-traditional insurance coverage or other risk mitigation procedures. Wildfire risks may be exacerbated by increasing temperatures and/or decreasing precipitation due to climate change.

paragraphs: Avista Corp., 在華盛頓州設立，於1889年成立，主要為電力與天然氣公用事業，並有其他商業投資。本公司總部位於華盛頓州的斯波肯市，為該州第二大城市。斯波肯市為內陸西北地區（東部華盛頓州與北部愛達荷州）的商業、運輸、醫療、工業與文化中心。區域服務包括政府與高等教育、醫療服務、零售貿易與金融。透過我們的子公司AEL&P，我們也提供電力公用事業服務於阿拉斯加朱安市。
截至2025年12月31日，我們有兩個應報告分部，如下：

• Avista Utilities – 為Avista Corp.的營運部門，包含在華盛頓州、愛達荷州、俄勒岡州與蒙大拿州的受規範公用事業營運。Avista Utilities在東部華盛頓州與北部愛達荷州的部分地區提供電力配電與輸電，以及天然氣配氣服務。Avista Utilities也在東北部與西南部俄勒岡州的部分地區提供天然氣配氣服務。Avista Utilities在華盛頓州、愛達荷州、俄勒岡州與蒙大拿州擁有電力發電設施。Avista Utilities也為蒙大拿州少數客戶提供電力服務。Avista Utilities也作為能源資源管理與負載服務義務的一部分，進行電力與天然氣的買賣。
• AEL&P – 為一受規範的公用事業，提供阿拉斯加朱安市的電力服務，為 wholly-owned subsidiary 並為AERC的主要營運子公司。
我們還有其他業務，包括風險投資基金投資、房地產投資，以及由Avista Capital所進行的其他投資，Avista Capital為Avista Corp.的直接、 wholly-owned subsidiary。這些活動並不代表應報告分部，且由Avista Corp.的各個直接與間接子公司進行。
截至2025年12月31日，Avista Corp.股東權益總額為2.7 十億美元，包含對Avista Capital的126 百萬美元投資，以及對AERC的129 百萬美元投資。
請參閱「財務會計彙編附註第24項」以取得各業務分部（及其他子公司）營運表現的資訊。
截至2025年12月31日，Avista Utilities僱用1,929名員工，其中談判單位員工佔總員工數的36％。
本公司對人才的作法是關鍵策略，用以激勵員工投入且蓬勃發展，透過建立一個員工被重視、被尊重且有成長機會的高績效組織。除了其他事項外，此策略支持招募優秀人才，並賦予他們能力、工具與文化，使其能追求卓越的想法。這些想法能激發想像力，並讓我們持續為客戶提供卓越且成本效益高的服務。此策略的重點領域致力於：
• 改進員工的參與度、歸屬感、公平性、吸引力與留存率，同時建立社區與使命感，
• 透過創新方案、最佳實務、工具與科技支持安全與員工福祉，以及
• 透過跨部門互動與外部網路擴展創新領域、能力與思維模式，以建構未來的價值。
以下為本公司部分關鍵人力資本方案的概覽，旨在激勵員工投入且蓬勃發展，以及其他利害關係人，例如客戶與商業夥伴。
AVISTA CORPORATION 員工吸引、發展與留存

paragraphs: 下列因素可能對我們的營運、營業成果、財務狀況或現金流產生重大影響。這些因素可能導致未來的結果或結果與我們在 SEC 檔案中所申報的報告（包括本年度 10-K 報告）及其他地方所討論的結果有顯著差異。請參閱 "前瞻性陳述" 以瞭解其他可能對我們營運、營業成果、財務狀況或現金流產生重大影響的因素，並可能導致實際結果與這些陳述中預期的結果有顯著差異。此外，尚有其他風險與不確定性，目前我們尚未知悉或目前認為不具重大性，也可能對我們產生不利影響。許多 herein 所討論的風險能否實現，取決於某些事件或情況的先前發生 – 即 "觸發條件"。我們可能或可能不會討論尚未導致對我們產生不利影響的觸發條件，且缺乏此類披露不應被視為表示未發生任何此類觸發條件。

Avista Utilities 的年度營運費用以及與增加投資於電力設施相關的成本，持續以快於營業收入的速率成長。我們能否回收這些費用與資本成本，取決於監管機構允許的零售電價調漲是否充足且及時，以及成本管理。我們預期會定期向監管機構申報電價調漲，以回收我們的費用與資本成本，並提供一個機會讓股東獲得合理的回報率。如果監管機構未來未批准電價調漲或批准的調漲幅度遠低於我們的請求，或如果無法回收遞延費用，或如果監管機構未允許我們回收與因符合新興法律與法規而必須退役或出售的資產相關的成本，可能會對我們的財務狀況、營業成果或現金流產生負面影響。請參閱 "項目 7. 管理層討論與分析 – 監管事項" 以進一步討論監管事項。
如果我們無法適用監管會計原則，我們可能：• 被要求核銷我們的監管資產，並被
• 禁止未來遞延成本或解耦收入，即使在這些金額發生時未透過電價回收，即使我們預期未來能從客戶處回收這些金額。
請參閱 "綜合財務陳述附註 1 – 監管遞延費用與信貸" 以進一步討論。

我們的設備可能是野火的點火源，或被認為是野火的起因。如果因我們的設備導致野火，我們可能被追究對生命與財產所造成損害的責任，以及滅火費用。此外，野火可能導致我們的設備出現延長的營運中斷，直到野火被撲滅後才能恢復供電，而對這些設施進行快速應對或修復的費用可能相當高昂。因我們的設備導致的野火可能對我們的聲譽造成重大損害，這可能會降低股東、客戶與社區的滿意度。此外，因我們的設備導致的野火可能導致訴訟與保險費用增加、保險覆蓋減少、需要自負風險或考慮非傳統保險覆蓋或其他風險緩釋措施。因氣候變遷導致的氣溫上升和/或降水量減少，可能使野火風險更加嚴重。
